questions.question: Under the Guidelines, who can qualify as a 'related party' of a designated person?
questions.answer: A related party includes a person acting on behalf of, at the direction of, or under the control of a designated person. A related party includes a person engaged in or providing support for proliferation‑sensitive activities and programmes, including through illicit means. A related party includes a person assisting the designated person in evading sanctions or violating resolution provisions. A related party includes a person with joint ownership of, or a beneficiary of, the assets (including property) of a designated person.

questions.question: What five general principles must a reporting institution ensure when combating ML/TF/PF under paragraph 6.2?
questions.answer: A reporting institution must ensure compliance with laws and regulations, conduct business in conformity with high ethical standards, and not provide services where there is good reason to suspect transactions are associated with ML/TF/PF activities. A reporting institution must co‑operate fully with relevant law enforcement agencies, including taking appropriate measures such as timely disclosure of information to the FIED and the relevant law enforcement agencies. A reporting institution must establish internal controls by issuing and adopting policies and procedures consistent with the AMLA, TFS‑PF related legislations and these Guidelines, and ensure ongoing training programmes for its board of directors, senior management and employees. A reporting institution must adopt a risk‑based approach, ensuring that the depth and breadth of its policies and procedures to identify, assess, monitor, manage and mitigate ML/TF/PF risks are commensurate with the nature, scale and complexity of its activities. A reporting institution must have an effective Customer Due Diligence procedure to identify its customers and obtain satisfactory evidence to verify their identity.

questions.question: What safeguards in paragraphs 11.13 to 11.16 support the compliance officer’s independence and central role in suspicious-transaction reporting?
questions.answer: Paragraph 11.13 requires the compliance officer to maintain a complete file of all internal reports on suspicious transactions and STRs lodged with FIED together with the relevant supporting documentary evidence, ensuring a documented record under the officer’s control. Paragraph 11.14 obliges the board of directors to ensure the compliance officer has the necessary authority, resources and support to discharge his obligations independently and effectively in complying with AML/CFT/CPF policies and procedures, safeguarding his independence. Paragraph 11.15 grants the compliance officer sole discretion and independence to report suspicious transactions, reinforcing his autonomous reporting role. Paragraph 11.16 designates the compliance officer as the central reference point within the organisation for all AML/CFT/CPF matters, establishing his central role in suspicious‑transaction reporting.

questions.question: Under Appendix B, how should a reporting institution treat family members or close associates of a PEP who no longer holds a prominent public function, and which factors may indicate continuing high risk?
questions.answer: A reporting institution should apply an appropriate risk assessment to family members or close associates of a PEP who no longer holds a prominent public function. In determining whether such a family member or close associate should be considered high risk, the institution may consider the level of informal influence the former PEP could still exercise. The institution may also consider whether the former PEP’s previous and current functions, although not in a public capacity, are linked by dealing with the same substantive matters.
questions.cited_answer: A reporting institution should apply an appropriate risk assessment to family members or close associates of a PEP who no longer holds a prominent public function. questions.question: What counter-proliferation-financing measures does Appendix G say Regulation 3 requires for designated countries and persons?
questions.answer: Regulation 3 requires the freezing of the funds and other financial assets or economic resources of designated countries or persons that are located in Malaysia.
